paper: APPSC Group-II Services Main Examination (Advt. No. 11/2023), Paper II: Indian & AP Economy and Science & Technology, held 23-02-2025 (Series A, 2G/202)

questions.s:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are incorrect regarding the GST Council (GSTC) ?
I. The GST Council is a constitutional body established under Article 269A of the Indian Constitution.
II. The GST Council is responsible for making recommendations on issues related to the Goods and Services Tax.
III. Every state does not have an equal vote in the GST Council.
IV. Decisions of the GST Council require a three-fourths majority of the weighted votes of the members present and voting.
questions.x: The GST Council is set up under Article 279A, not 269A, and every State has an equal vote in it, so I and III are incorrect. II and IV correctly describe its role and its three-fourths weighted-majority rule.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: The severe balance of payments crisis, faced by India in 1991 was characterized by
o: High inflation, low foreign exchange reserves and a large fiscal deficit
Rapid industrial growth, increased foreign exchange reserves and a trade surplus
Low inflation, high foreign exchange reserves and a balanced fiscal budget
Strong foreign investment inflows, low inflation and fiscal deficit
questions.x: In 1991 India had double-digit inflation, forex reserves covering only about two weeks of imports and a fiscal deficit near 8 per cent of GDP.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding PURVODAYA scheme introduced by the Government of India in 2024 ?
I. The PURVODAYA scheme aims to improve infrastructure in the eastern part of India.
II. It deals with Buxar-Bhagalpur Expressway.
III. New Delhi-Kolkata Industrial Corridor is being developed as part of the PURVODAYA scheme.
IV. The primary goal of this scheme is the development of Gujarat State.
questions.x: Purvodaya, announced in the July 2024 Budget, targets the eastern States, and the Buxar-Bhagalpur expressway was among the Bihar projects announced. The industrial corridor named in the Budget was Amritsar-Kolkata, not New Delhi-Kolkata, and Gujarat is not covered.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s:
Which of the following statements accurately describe the environmental impacts associated with agricultural practices ?
I. The application of synthetic fertilizers and pesticides may result in soil and water contamination.
II. Sustainable agriculture focuses on preserving soil health and protecting biodiversity.
III. Modern agricultural practices are unrelated to the depletion of freshwater resources.
IV. Expanding monoculture farming supports overall ecosystem stability.
questions.x: Agrochemicals can pollute soil and water, and sustainable farming aims to protect soil health and biodiversity. Modern irrigation-heavy farming depletes freshwater, and monocultures reduce ecosystem stability.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: What was the primary reason for the current account surplus in Q4:2023-24 ?
questions.x: RBI data showed India's current account surplus of 0.6 per cent of GDP in January-March 2024 was driven mainly by strong net services exports, along with a narrower merchandise trade deficit.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Post-economic reforms, the Indian economy saw a shift towards
questions.x: The 1991 LPG reforms opened India to trade and foreign investment, integrating it much more with the global economy.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s:
Which of the following statements is/are correct about Foreign Portfolio Investments (FPI) in 2024-25 ?
I. The Indian Rupee (INR) moved in a narrow range with low volatility despite FPI outflows.
II. RBI set investment limits for FPIs in debt instruments and Credit Default Swaps.
III. FPI investment limits in government securities and corporate bonds remained unchanged.
IV. RBI issued an operation framework for reclassification of FPI investments beyond permitted limits.
questions.x: In 2024-25 the rupee stayed relatively stable despite FPI outflows, RBI kept FPI debt limits unchanged and set limits for FPIs in debt and CDS, and in November 2024 it issued a framework to reclassify FPI holdings above 10 per cent as FDI. All four statements are correct.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Which of the following is not a method of measurement of National Income ?
questions.x: National income is measured by the product (value added), income and expenditure methods. There is no 'cost and accounting' method.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s:
Which of the following are the major provisions of the Industrial Policy Resolution 1956 ?
I. Provision of licencing.
II. Expansion of public sector.
III. Emphasis on small industries.
questions.x: The 1956 Resolution classified industries into three schedules with a dominant public sector, kept industrial licensing, and stressed the role of cottage and small industries.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: The part of investment (Increase or Decrease) which takes place due to change in the level of national income is termed as
questions.x: Induced investment varies with income (the accelerator effect), while autonomous investment does not depend on the level of income.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Which of the following statements is False ?
o: Exchange rate is the rate at which the currency of one country exchanges for the currency of another country
A direct quote is the number of units of a foreign currency exchangeable for one unit of home currency
An exchange rate regime is the system by which a country manages its currency with respect to foreign currencies
There are two major types of exchange rate regime : floating exchange rate and fixed exchange rate
questions.x: A direct quote gives the units of home currency per unit of foreign currency (for example Rs 84 = $1). The definition in (2) is the indirect quote.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s:
Statement A : The GoI fiscal deficit R E for 2024-25 is 4.8% of GDP.
Statement B : It is higher than the Fiscal Deficit B E for 2025 - 2026.
o: Neither A nor B is correct
questions.x: The Union Budget 2025-26 put the 2024-25 revised estimate of the fiscal deficit at 4.8 per cent of GDP and set the 2025-26 budget estimate lower, at 4.4 per cent.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Which principal methodology is employed by the National Statistical Office (NSO) as the standard mechanism for assessing and quantifying the unemployment rate within the Indian economy ?
questions.x: Since 2017 the NSO has measured unemployment through the Periodic Labour Force Survey.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Which among the following classifications of unemployment is predominantly correlated with the agricultural sector ?
questions.x: Farm work peaks at sowing and harvest, so agricultural labourers are typically idle in the off-season. That is seasonal unemployment.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: How does the introduction of the Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) enhance the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) liquidity management framework ?
o: By increasing the overall liquidity in the banking system
By absorbing surplus liquidity without the need for collateral
By keeping the cost of liquidity for commercial banks constant
By providing long-term loans to banks at lower interest rates
questions.x: The SDF, introduced in 2022 as the floor of the LAF corridor, lets RBI absorb surplus liquidity without giving government securities as collateral, unlike reverse repo.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s:
What is/are the goal(s) of SEBI's new move to introduce T+0 settlement ?
I. To enhance liquidity and reduce settlement risk in the stock market.
II. To minimize counter party risk and enhance market efficiency.
III. Potentially reduce the impact of market volatility on settlement.
IV. To increase operational expenses for market participants.
questions.x: Same-day (T+0) settlement aims to improve liquidity, cut settlement and counterparty risk and limit volatility exposure. Raising costs for participants is not a goal.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Which of the following mechanisms is NOT primarily followed by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to manage exchange rate volatility ?
questions.x: Fiscal policy belongs to the government, not RBI. RBI manages exchange-rate volatility through its forex reserves and market intervention within the market-based exchange rate system.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: What is the significance of the new payment settlement framework introduced by the RBI in the context of the Foreign Trade Policy 2023 ?
o: It discourages the use of the Indian currency in cross-border trade
It aims to encourage the use of the Indian currency in cross-border trade
It eliminates the need for foreign exchange reserves
It increases transaction costs for exporters
questions.x: RBI's mechanism for invoicing and settling trade in rupees (through Special Rupee Vostro Accounts), backed by the Foreign Trade Policy 2023, aims to internationalise the rupee.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Which Article of the Indian Constitution empowers the Central Government to extend loans to State Governments ?
questions.x: Article 293(2) lets the Government of India make loans to any State, subject to limits set by Parliament. Article 292 covers the Union's own borrowing.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: India's rank in World Bank's Logistic Performance Index in 2023
questions.x: India ranked 38th of 139 countries in the World Bank's Logistics Performance Index 2023, up from 44th in 2018.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: What impact does an increase in the GNP deflator have on the purchasing power of money ?
questions.x: A rising GNP deflator means a higher general price level, so each unit of money buys less.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Which organization launched the Credit Guarantee Scheme for the Livestock Sector ?
o: Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying
questions.x: The Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying launched the Credit Guarantee Scheme for the livestock sector in 2024 under its Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: When currency is bought at a lower price at one place in the foreign exchange market and at the same time sold at a higher price at another place, this process is called
questions.x: Arbitrage means buying where the price is lower and selling at the same time where it is higher, to profit from the price difference.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Special Drawing Rights is the currency of International Monetary Fund. This is in the form of
questions.x: SDRs are an IMF reserve asset that exists only as book entries in members' accounts; no notes or coins are issued. That is why they are called 'paper gold'.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s:
Which of the following are included in the Reserve Bank of India's Foreign Exchange Reserves (FER) ?
a. Foreign Currency Assets (FCA)
b. Gold
c. Special Drawing Rights (SDR)
d. Reserve Tranche Position
questions.x: India's forex reserves are made up of foreign currency assets, gold, SDRs and the reserve tranche position in the IMF.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s:
Which of the following factors could potentially contribute to stagflation in the Indian economy ?
a. High inflationary pressures due to increased Government spending.
b. Decline in industrial production and sluggish economic growth.
c. Decrease in aggregate demand and consumer spending.
d. Appreciation of the domestic currency leading to reduction of export competitiveness.
questions.x: Stagflation combines inflation with stagnant output. The key treats all four factors (inflationary spending, falling production, weak demand and loss of export competitiveness) as possible contributors.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s:
As per the Economic Survey, 2023, which of the following statements correctly describe(s) the trend of Foreign Direct Investment in India ?
a. It has decreased due to less participation of the private sector.
b. It has increased compared to the prepandemic levels.
c. It has increased rapidly without decreasing in any Financial Year after the telecom sector was entirely reformed.
d. It has decreased due to a weak global economic situation.
questions.x: The Economic Survey 2022-23 noted that FDI inflows fell in 2022 because of the weak and uncertain global economic situation, in line with the global trend.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Which of the following is not true about globalization and its impact on India ?
o: It has expanded trade in goods and services
It has led to greater flow of Foreign Direct Investment
Increase in exports is greater than increase in imports
Increased India's access to foreign technology and investment
questions.x: Since liberalisation India's imports have grown faster than its exports, which is why it has run a persistent trade deficit. Statement (3) is therefore not true.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Which of the following statements about non-plan expenditures of the Central Government is correct ?
o: The expenditure is on interest payments
The expenditure is on science and technology
questions.x: Under the old plan/non-plan classification, interest payments were the largest non-plan item. Spending on sectors such as agriculture and science was largely plan expenditure.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s:
Which of the following statements is/are correct ?
a. India's overall SDG score has improved to 71 in 2023-24, Uttarakhand shares the top spot with Kerala, both scored above India's overall SDG score.
b. In the latest SDG India Index 2023-24, Andhra Pradesh is placed in the "Front Runner" category.
c. Arunachal Pradesh and Meghalaya, each with scores above 75, are placed in the "Achiever" category.
d. In the 2023-2024 SDG Index, Lakshadweep and Uttar Pradesh scored significantly above the national average, demonstrating notable progress compared to other states.
questions.x: In NITI Aayog's SDG India Index 2023-24 India scored 71, Kerala and Uttarakhand topped with 79, and Andhra Pradesh was a Front Runner. Arunachal and Meghalaya were not Achievers, and statement d is also wrong.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: What item(s) account for the differences between GDP at factor cost and GDP at market prices ?
questions.x: GDP at market prices equals GDP at factor cost plus indirect taxes minus subsidies.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s:
Assertion (A): Devaluation will lead to improvement in balance of trade.
Reason (R) : Devaluation will lead to increase in price of exports.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.x: Devaluation makes exports cheaper and imports dearer for foreigners, which tends to improve the trade balance. It lowers export prices, so (R) is false.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: A person who has ultimate control over the affairs of a factory under Factories Act, 1948 is called
questions.x: Section 2(n) of the Factories Act, 1948 defines the occupier as the person who has ultimate control over the affairs of the factory.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: A budgeting process which demands each manager to justify his entire budget in detail from beginning is
questions.x: Zero-base budgeting starts each budget from zero, so every item must be justified afresh rather than carried forward from the previous year.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: GDP deflator is the most comprehensive measure of inflation as it is the ratio of
o: GDP at National prices to Local prices
GDP at Low prices to High prices
GDP at Current prices to Constant prices
questions.x: The GDP deflator is nominal GDP (current prices) divided by real GDP (constant prices). It covers all goods and services produced, which makes it the broadest price measure.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Which of the following measures is NOT typically used to correct a disequilibrium in the Balance of Payments (BOP) ?
o: Reducing government spending on domestic projects
questions.x: Devaluation, import tariffs and attracting FDI are standard BoP correction tools. Cutting domestic project spending is a fiscal measure and not a typical direct BoP remedy.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Which among the following statements is correct ?
o: Balance of payments includes current account and capital account
Balance of payments includes only capital account
Balance of payments includes only current account
Balance of payments includes only export and import account
questions.x: The balance of payments records all of a country's transactions with the rest of the world in two main parts, the current account and the capital account.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s:
Assertion (A): Transfer earnings are not to be included in the estimation of National Income.
Reason (R) : Transfer earnings are not payments for factor services.
o: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct, but (R) is not correct
(R) is correct, but (A) is not correct
questions.x: National income counts only incomes earned for productive (factor) services. Transfer payments such as pensions and subsidies are unearned, so they are excluded.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s:
Match List - I with List - II and choose correct answer. (Common codes for English and Telugu Versions)
List - I / List - II
a. Monetary Policy - i. Tax Rate
b. Trade Policy - ii. Margin
c. Credit Policy - iii. Imports and Exports
d. Fiscal Policy - iv. Bank Rate
questions.x: The bank rate is a monetary policy tool, trade policy governs imports and exports, margin requirements are a selective credit control, and tax rates are a fiscal tool.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: The situation where a country simultaneously imports and exports the same product is called
questions.x: Intra-industry trade is the two-way exchange of similar products, such as a country both exporting and importing cars.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: What challenges does India face in managing its oil consumption ?
o: Supply chain disruptions and fluctuating global oil prices
questions.x: India imports over 85 per cent of its crude oil, so it is exposed to supply disruptions and volatile world oil prices.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Under the Industrial Policy of 1991
o: The mandatory convertible clause is applicable to all term loans
The mandatory convertible clause is applicable to term loans of more than 10 years
The mandatory convertible clause is applicable to term loans of less than 10 years
The mandatory convertible clause is no longer applicable
questions.x: The 1991 Industrial Policy dropped the requirement that financial institutions' term loans carry a clause allowing conversion of the debt into equity.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Which of the following are used for measuring of the high-power money supply (H) by RBI in India ?
o: Currency held by the public + Other deposits with the RBI
Cash reserves of the commercial banks + Other deposits with the RBI
Currency held by the public + Cash reserves of the commercial banks + Other deposits with the RBI
Currency held by the public + Cash reserves of the commercial banks + Time deposits of the commercial banks + Other deposits with the RBI
questions.x: Reserve money (high-powered money, M0) is currency with the public plus banks' cash reserves (cash in hand and deposits with RBI) plus other deposits with RBI.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Which of the following reforms have contributed to the improvement of the Ease of Doing Business in India ?
o: The introduction of GST (Goods and Services Tax)
Removal of all foreign ownership restrictions in Indian companies
Expansion of public sector enterprises into new sectors
questions.x: GST replaced many indirect taxes with one, simplifying compliance and inter-state trade. The other options either never happened or would not ease business.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s:
There is no GST on which of the following ?
i. Petrol and Diesel
ii. Liquor
iii. Electricity supply to consumers
iv. Services of Charitable entities
questions.x: Petrol and diesel are currently outside GST, alcohol for human consumption is excluded constitutionally, and electricity supply and specified charitable services are exempt. So none of the four attracts GST.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s:
Assertion (A) : India's real Gross Domestic Product (GDP) grew by 8.2% in FY24 despite global and external challenges.
Reason (R) : The focus on maintaining macroeconomic stability ensured that these challenges had minimal impact on India's economy.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.x: The Economic Survey 2023-24 reported 8.2 per cent real GDP growth in FY24 and credited the focus on macroeconomic stability with limiting the impact of external shocks.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Which Indian organization is responsible for estimating the National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) ?
questions.x: NITI Aayog prepares India's National Multidimensional Poverty Index, using NFHS data and the Oxford-UNDP methodology.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s:
Assertion (A) : The Indian economy demonstrated resilience despite global geopolitical challenges.
Reason (R) : India's fiscal and monetary policies ensured economic and financial stability post-COVID.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.x: The Economic Survey attributes India's resilience amid geopolitical shocks to post-COVID fiscal and monetary policies that kept the economy and financial system stable.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: What was the purpose of the 49 fine-tuning operations conducted by the RBI during FY 2024 ?
o: To maintain liquidity conditions in alignment with the monetary policy stance
questions.x: RBI's fine-tuning variable rate repo and reverse repo operations inject or absorb liquidity as needed, keeping liquidity in line with the monetary policy stance.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s:
Statement A : The RBI announced a temporary I-CRR of 10 per cent on 10 August 2023.
Statement B : This action impounded about Rs. 1.1 lakh crores from the banking system.
o: Both statements A and B are correct
Both statements A and B are incorrect
questions.x: On 10 August 2023 RBI imposed a 10 per cent incremental CRR on deposit growth, which absorbed about Rs 1.1 lakh crore of surplus liquidity. Both statements are correct.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s:
Statement A : India is the largest producer of milk.
Statement B : India is the second largest producer of fruits, vegetables and sugar.
o: Both statements A and B are correct
Both statements A and B are incorrect
questions.x: India is the world's largest milk producer and second only to China in fruits and vegetables. The key also treats it as second in sugar.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: At what subsidized price per Kg did the Government introduce "Bharat Rice" for selling through NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar ?
questions.x: Bharat Rice was launched in February 2024 at Rs 29 per kg, sold through NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar outlets.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Which initiative was launched to provide a tap water connection to every rural household by 2024 ?
questions.x: The Jal Jeevan Mission, launched in 2019, aimed to give every rural household a functional household tap connection by 2024.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s:
Match the sectors given in Column - A with their corresponding Gross Value Added (GVA) Growth Rates given in Column - B (Andhra Pradesh Advance Estimates of 2023-24). (Common codes for English and Telugu Versions)
Column - A / Column - B
a. Agriculture and allied activities - A. 5.21%
b. Industry - B. 8.02%
c. Services - C. 1.69%
questions.x: AP's advance estimates for 2023-24 showed GVA growth of about 1.69 per cent in agriculture and allied sectors, 8.02 per cent in industry and 5.21 per cent in services (as given in the Socio-Economic Survey).
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s:
Statement A : All India Per Capita Income for the year 2023-24 (PE) is estimated at Rs.1,84,205.
Statement B : All India Per Capita Income given above is lower than the Andhra Pradesh Per Capita Income for the year 2023-24 (AE) (at current prices from 2014-15 to 2023-24).
o: Both statements A and B are correct
Both statements A and B are incorrect
questions.x: India's per capita income at current prices for 2023-24 was about Rs 1.84 lakh, while AP's 2023-24 advance estimate was about Rs 2.42 lakh, which is higher. Both statements are correct.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s:
Statement A : Andhra Pradesh ranks 1st in the productivity of Oil palm in India.
Statement B : Andhra Pradesh ranks 2nd in the productivity of Mango in India.
o: Both statements A and B are correct
Both statements A and B are incorrect
questions.x: According to the AP Socio-Economic Survey, the State ranks first in oil palm productivity and second in mango productivity in India.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: How many Rythu Bharosa Kendralu (RBKs) has the Government of Andhra Pradesh established according to Socio-Economic Survey of Andhra Pradesh 2023-24 ?
questions.x: The AP Socio-Economic Survey 2023-24 reports 10,778 Rythu Bharosa Kendras set up at village level to provide one-stop farm services.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: As per the second advanced estimates of National Statistical Office (NSO), MoSPI, GOI, what is the sector wise contribution of GVA at current prices for the year 2022-23 for Andhra Pradesh ?
questions.x: For 2022-23 AP's GVA at current prices was about 36.19 per cent agriculture and allied, 23.36 per cent industry and 40.45 per cent services. Agriculture's share is far above the national average.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: According to the report on Relative Economic Performance of Indian States (1960-61 to 2023-24), prepared by Economic Advisory Council to the PM, what are the individual shares of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana in the National GDP in FY 2023-24 ?
questions.x: The EAC-PM paper (September 2024) put Andhra Pradesh's share of national GDP in 2023-24 at 4.7 per cent and Telangana's at 4.9 per cent.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s:
Statement A : In AP, capital expenditure constituted less than 15 per cent in the total Government expenditure during 2016-21.
Statement B : Capital expenditure reflects the State's commitment towards infrastructure creation.
o: A is true, but B is false
A is false, but B is true
Both A and B are true
Both A and B are false
questions.x: CAG/State finance data show AP's capital expenditure stayed below 15 per cent of total expenditure in 2016-21, and capital spending is the usual indicator of a State's investment in infrastructure. Both statements are true.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: In the Union Budget 2024-25, the GOI has promised funds to the following industrial nodes as part of the development of the Vishakhapatnam-Chennai and Bangalore-Hyderabad industrial corridors
questions.x: The July 2024 Budget promised funds for the Kopparthy node on the Visakhapatnam-Chennai corridor and the Orvakal node on the Hyderabad-Bengaluru corridor.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: As per the Budget estimates of 2024-25, the percentage of public debt in the GSDP of Andhra Pradesh in FY 2024-25 is estimated as
questions.x: The AP Budget 2024-25 estimated the State's outstanding public debt at about 34.14 per cent of GSDP.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s:
Match the following Central Institutes established under the A. P. State Reorganization Act, 2014 with their locations. (Common codes for English and Telugu Versions)
a. Indian Institute of Technology - i. Kurnool
b. Indian Institute of Management - ii. Tirupati
c. All India Institute of Medical Sciences - iii. Vizianagaram
d. Indian Institute of Information Technology - iv. Vijayawada
e. Tribal University - v. Vishakhapatnam
questions.x: Under the Act, IIT came up at Tirupati, IIM at Visakhapatnam, AIIMS at Mangalagiri near Vijayawada, IIITDM at Kurnool and the Central Tribal University at Vizianagaram.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Which of the following is not correct regarding the railway project under Central Assistance approved by the Union Cabinet for Amaravati in Andhra Pradesh ?
o: The proposed railway line is between Errupalem and Nambur
The cost of the project is Rs. 2,245 crores for 57 km
The line passes through NTR and Guntur Districts in Andhra Pradesh and Khammam District in Telangana
The proposed time line of the project is 6 years
questions.x: The Errupalem-Amaravati-Nambur line (57 km, Rs 2,245 crore) approved in October 2024 is to be completed in 4 years, not 6.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s:
Match the following minerals (List - I) with the erstwhile districts (List - II) where they are predominantly available. (Common codes for English and Telugu Versions)
List - I / List - II
a. Apatite - i. West Godavari
b. Asbestos - ii. Nellore
c. Ball Clay - iii. Visakhapatnam
d. Mica - iv. Kadapa
questions.x: Apatite occurs in Visakhapatnam, asbestos in Kadapa (Pulivendula), ball clay in West Godavari and mica in the Nellore mica belt.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Which International funding agencies committed to fund the Amaravati Capital City Phase-I Development in Andhra Pradesh ?
o: World Bank and Asian Development Bank
questions.x: In 2024 the World Bank and the Asian Development Bank jointly committed about US$1.6 billion for Amaravati Capital City Phase-I.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Which external funding agency is supporting the Andhra Pradesh Integrated Irrigation and Agriculture Transformation Project ?
questions.x: The AP Integrated Irrigation and Agriculture Transformation Project (APIIATP) is World Bank-assisted and covers tank-based irrigation and climate-resilient farming.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s:
Match the following irrigation projects (List - I) with the rivers on which they are located (List - II). (Common codes for English and Telugu Versions)
List - I / List - II
a. Somasila reservoir - i. Cheyyeru
b. Thotapally project - ii. Penna
c. Annamayya project - iii. Manneru
d. Rallapadu - iv. Nagavali
questions.x: Somasila is on the Penna, Thotapalli on the Nagavali, Annamayya on the Cheyyeru and Rallapadu on the Manneru.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s:
Assertion (A) : In Andhra Pradesh, the coverage of farmers under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana has been increasing over the years.
Reason (R) : In Andhra Pradesh, significant crop losses occurred to farmers due to extreme weather events in recent years including floods, droughts and cyclones.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.x: Repeated floods, droughts and cyclones caused heavy crop losses in AP, which pushed up farmer enrolment in crop insurance under PMFBY. The key treats (R) as the explanation of (A).
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Which is not a correct statement regarding Rytu Bazaars in Andhra Pradesh ?
o: Rytu Bazaars were established in the year 1999
District Collector is the Co-ordinating officer of Rytu Bazaars
Rytu Bazaar is managed by an Estate Officer
The prices in Rytu Bazaar are fixed aiming to be around 25% above wholesale prices and 25% below the local retail prices
questions.x: Rythu Bazaars started in 1999, each run by an Estate Officer, with prices set about 25 per cent above wholesale and 25 per cent below retail. The district-level coordinating officer is the Joint Collector, not the District Collector.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Chadalawada village where a Cattle Breeding farm is established under Gokul Gram Project under Rashtriya Gokula Mission belongs to which District ?
questions.x: The Gokul Gram for indigenous Ongole cattle under the Rashtriya Gokul Mission is at Chadalawada in Prakasam district.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s:
Match the following Special Economic Zone Production Units in (List-I) with their locations (List-II). (Common codes for English and Telugu Versions)
List - I / List - II
a. Divi's Laboratories Limited-Pharmaceuticals - i. Nellore
b. Parry Infrastructure Company-Food Processing - ii. Kovvur
c. White Field Paper Mills Ltd.-Writing and Printing Paper - iii. Kakinada
d. Indian Farmers Fertilizers Co-operative Ltd. (IFFCO)-Multi Products - iv. Visakhapatnam
questions.x: Divi's pharma SEZ is near Visakhapatnam, Parry's food-processing SEZ is at Kakinada, the White Field paper SEZ is at Kovvur and the IFFCO Kisan SEZ is in Nellore.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Which of the following is not the target of AP Electronics Manufacturing Policy (4.0), 2024-29 ?
o: Increase production in the State to USD 50 Billion
First time employment creation of 5 lakhs
First time entrepreneurship creation of 2 lakhs
questions.x: The AP Electronics Manufacturing Policy 4.0 targets USD 50 billion of output, USD 10 billion of investment and 5 lakh jobs. Creating 2 lakh first-time entrepreneurs is not among its targets.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: According to AP Industrial Policy (4.0), 2024-29 one of the following statements is not correct with regard to MSME sector in Andhra Pradesh.
o: AP accounts for 9 lakh registered MSMEs as on February 2024 according to Udyam data base
Majority of the MSMEs are concentrated in service sector accounting for 79%
There are 28 exclusive MSME parks in AP
The MSME sector is contributing 33.5% of GSDP in AP
questions.x: The policy figures for registered MSMEs, the services share and MSME parks are correct, but it does not credit MSMEs with 33.5 per cent of AP's GSDP; that figure is wrong.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: One of the following is not the standard incentive to the industries offered by Government of AP based on the AP Industrial Policy (4.0), 2024-29.
o: 100% stamp duty reimbursement on purchase of land and lease of land/shed/buildings
Reimbursement of 100% fee charged for land conversion
Maximum capital subsidy of 15% of Foreign capital investment
questions.x: The policy's standard incentives include a decarbonisation subsidy, full stamp-duty reimbursement and land-conversion fee reimbursement. A 15 per cent capital subsidy on foreign capital investment is not one of them.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: What is the primary goal of India's National Clean Energy Fund (NCEF) ?
o: Promote renewable energy technologies and reduce carbon emissions
questions.x: The NCEF, financed by a cess on coal from 2010, was created to fund clean and renewable energy research and projects that cut carbon emissions.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: National Green Tribunal (NGT) was established to
o: Handle cases related to environmental protection and pollution control
questions.x: The NGT was set up under the NGT Act, 2010 for speedy disposal of cases on environmental protection, forest conservation and pollution.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s:
Match the pollution type with its major source. (Common codes for English & Telugu Versions)
Pollution Type / Major Source
a. Air Pollution - I. Sewage
b. Water Pollution - II. Industrial emissions
c. Soil Pollution - III. Use of chemical fertilizers
d. Noise Pollution - IV. Construction activities
questions.x: Industrial emissions pollute air, sewage pollutes water, chemical fertilisers pollute soil and construction activity is a major noise source.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: Which of the following methods is used for solid waste disposal in urban areas of India ?
questions.x: Indian cities use composting, incineration (waste-to-energy) and landfilling, so all three methods apply.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: Which of the following is the primary goal of India's "Municipal Solid Waste Management and Handling Rules, 2000" ?
questions.x: The MSW (Management and Handling) Rules, 2000 required municipalities to segregate waste at source and collect and process it scientifically.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: What is the main advantage of organic farming over conventional farming ?
o: Higher crop yields in all conditions
Reduced chemical input and improved soil health
questions.x: Organic farming avoids synthetic fertilisers and pesticides and builds soil organic matter, improving soil health.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: What is the primary source of air pollution in Indian cities ?
questions.x: Vehicle exhaust is the largest contributor to urban air pollution in most Indian cities.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: Which of the following is NOT an example of a bioremediation technique ?
questions.x: Bioremediation uses living organisms such as microbes or plants to break down pollutants. Burning soil is a thermal treatment, not a biological one.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: What was the primary purpose of the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981 ?
questions.x: The Air Act, 1981 was enacted to prevent, control and abate air pollution and to maintain air quality through pollution control boards.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: Which of the following government initiatives aims to control industrial emissions in India ?
o: Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT)
questions.x: The National Clean Air Programme (2019) aims to cut particulate pollution in non-attainment cities, including by controlling industrial emissions.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: Which of the following is NOT an alternative to conventional pollution control methods ?
questions.x: Incineration is itself a conventional waste-disposal method. Green technology, bioremediation and carbon capture are newer alternatives.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: What is the primary environmental concern associated with Genetically Modified (GM) crops ?
questions.x: Gene flow from GM crops to conventional crops and wild relatives through cross-pollination is the main ecological worry.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: Which Organization regulates Genetically Modified Organisms (GMOs) in India ?
o: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI)
questions.x: The GEAC under the Environment Ministry approves the environmental release of GM organisms under the 1989 Rules.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: Which of the following is an example of an environmentally friendly technology used in agriculture ?
questions.x: Organic farming relies on natural inputs and avoids synthetic chemicals, making it environmentally friendly.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: Which technology can reduce the environmental impact of traditional farming, especially in water scarce regions ?
questions.x: Drip irrigation delivers water straight to plant roots, saving water and reducing waterlogging and salinity.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: What is the primary application of bioremediation ?
questions.x: Bioremediation is mainly used to clean contaminated soil (and groundwater) by letting microbes or plants degrade the pollutants.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: Which of the following bioremediation techniques is used to treat oil spills ?
questions.x: Bioaugmentation adds specialised oil-degrading microbes to a spill site to speed up hydrocarbon breakdown.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s:
Match the following : (Common codes for English & Telugu Versions)
Waste Type / Appropriate Disposal Method
a. Organic Waste - I. Incineration
b. E-waste - II. Composting
c. Hazardous Waste - III. Landfilling
d. Broken glass pieces - IV. Recycling
questions.x: Organic waste is composted, e-waste recycled, hazardous waste incinerated, and broken glass pieces go to landfill.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s:
Match the following : (Common codes for English & Telugu Versions)
Waste Disposal Method / Pros/Cons
a. Landfilling - I. Low-cost, but has long-term environmental impact
b. Incineration - II. Reduces volume of waste, but emits pollutants
c. Composting - III. Produces useful by-products like biogas, but requires land
d. Recycling - IV. Conserves resources, but needs infrastructure
questions.x: Landfilling is cheap but has lasting impacts, incineration cuts volume but emits pollutants, composting yields useful products but needs land, and recycling saves resources but needs infrastructure.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: Which Indian city is recognized for adopting zero waste concept in solid waste management ?
questions.x: Indore, repeatedly ranked India's cleanest city in Swachh Survekshan, is known for its zero-waste model based on full segregation and processing.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: Which of the following is a potential tipping point of global climate change ?
questions.x: Loss of Arctic sea ice is a recognised climate tipping element: less ice reflects less sunlight, which speeds further warming in a self-reinforcing loop.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: The "ozone hole" is primarily caused by the release of
questions.x: Chlorine released from CFCs in the stratosphere breaks down ozone catalytically, producing the Antarctic ozone hole.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: Which International Agreement does not focus on reducing greenhouse gas emissions to combat climate change ?
questions.x: The Basel Convention (1989) controls the cross-border movement of hazardous wastes and has nothing to do with emissions. The key treats the Montreal Protocol as relevant, since its Kigali Amendment phases down HFC greenhouse gases.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: India's National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC) aims to address
o: Mitigation and adaptation strategies for climate change
questions.x: The NAPCC (2008) sets out national missions covering both mitigation and adaptation to climate change.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: What is the key characteristic of black carbon that accelerates global warming ?
o: It is a type of methane
It is a short-lived pollutant produced by incomplete combustion
It directly depletes the ozone layer
questions.x: Black carbon (soot) from incomplete burning of fuels and biomass is a short-lived climate pollutant that absorbs sunlight and darkens snow and ice.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: Which of the following countries is/are legally bound by the emissions reduction targets set by the Paris Agreement ?
questions.x: Under the Paris Agreement each party sets its own nationally determined contribution, and the emission targets themselves are not legally binding on any country.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: How many core missions are included in India's National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC) ?
questions.x: The NAPCC launched eight national missions, including Solar, Enhanced Energy Efficiency, Sustainable Habitat, Water, Himalayan Ecosystem, Green India, Sustainable Agriculture and Strategic Knowledge.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: What is the "dual burden" India faces in public health ?
o: Rising rates of both infectious and non-communicable diseases
Lack of insurance and financial access
High rates of both obesity and malnutrition
questions.x: APPSC's key takes the 'double burden of malnutrition': undernutrition and obesity existing side by side in the population.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: The concept of sustainable development was first popularized by which report ?
questions.x: The Brundtland Commission's 1987 report 'Our Common Future' popularised sustainable development as meeting present needs without compromising future generations.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: What is a key goal of sustainable development ?
o: Economic growth with no concern for environmental impacts
Ensuring social equity, economic growth and environmental protection
Promoting environmental conservation over all else
questions.x: Sustainable development seeks a balance of economic growth, social equity and environmental protection.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: Which of the following is not one of the three pillars of sustainability ?
questions.x: The three pillars of sustainability are environmental, economic and social. Political sustainability is not one of them.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: How many Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) has the United Nations established ?
questions.x: The UN's 2030 Agenda, adopted in 2015, contains 17 Sustainable Development Goals with 169 targets.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: Subject that is not associated with Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission
questions.x: ABDM's building blocks include the ABHA health ID, the Healthcare Professionals Registry and a technology Sandbox. Arogya Mitras are frontline helpers under the PM-JAY insurance scheme, not ABDM.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: Which of the following is true about the "Circular Economy" ?
o: It focuses on reducing the use of fossil fuels
It promotes the reuse, recycling and repair of materials to reduce waste
It focuses exclusively on reducing carbon emissions
questions.x: A circular economy keeps materials in use through reuse, repair and recycling, unlike the linear take-make-dispose model.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: Which global summit led to the adoption of the "Agenda 21" and the "Rio Declaration" ?
questions.x: Agenda 21 and the Rio Declaration were adopted at the UN Conference on Environment and Development (Earth Summit) in Rio de Janeiro in 1992.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: Which of the following public health campaigns was launched to improve sanitation in India ?
questions.x: Swachh Bharat Abhiyan, launched on 2 October 2014, targeted sanitation and an open-defecation-free India.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: Ayushman Bharat primarily aims to provide healthcare coverage to which group ?
questions.x: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY gives Rs 5 lakh a year of hospital cover to poor and vulnerable families identified mainly from SECC data.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: Which of the following factors contributed most to the burden of malnutrition in India ?
o: Lack of access to clean water
Poor dietary habits and food insecurity
questions.x: Inadequate and poor-quality diets caused by food insecurity are the main driver of malnutrition in India.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: What is Digital arrest ?
o: Arrest made by police when the accused is in foreign countries
Arrest made by police when the accused cannot be arrested physically
Arrest made by police when the accused is granted anticipatory bail by courts
Term used by cyber criminals to scare victims
questions.x: 'Digital arrest' is a cyber-fraud tactic in which criminals pose as police or officials on video calls and threaten victims with fake arrest to extort money. Indian law has no such procedure.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s:
The mission of the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) is
a. Energy Security
b. Increase in the share of clean power
c. Energy availability and access
d. Energy affordability
e. Energy equity
o: Only a, c, d and e
questions.x: MNRE's mission statement covers energy security, a higher share of clean power, energy availability and access, affordability and equity, so all five apply.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: India has the ________ largest installed wind power capacity in the world.
questions.x: India ranks fourth in the world in installed wind power capacity, after China, the USA and Germany.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV) launchers have
o: One solid rocket motor stage, one earth storable liquid stage and one cryogenic stage
First and third stage solid rocket motors and second and fourth stages liquid rocket motors
Three liquid stage motors and one solid stage motors
One liquid stage motor and three solid stage motors
questions.x: GSLV is a three-stage vehicle: a solid core first stage (with liquid strap-ons), an earth-storable liquid second stage and a cryogenic upper stage. Option (2) describes the PSLV.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: BrahMos supersonic cruise missile is developed by the joint efforts of
questions.x: BrahMos is built by BrahMos Aerospace, a joint venture of India's DRDO and Russia's NPO Mashinostroyeniya; the name joins the Brahmaputra and Moskva rivers.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: The terms 'Petya' and 'WannaCry' are related to
questions.x: WannaCry and Petya/NotPetya were ransomware attacks in 2017 that encrypted computers worldwide and demanded payment.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: CITES (Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora) is also known as
questions.x: CITES was signed in Washington D.C. in 1973 and is therefore also called the Washington Convention.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: Which of the following chemicals was released in the Bhopal disaster of 1984 ?
questions.x: The December 1984 Union Carbide disaster at Bhopal released methyl isocyanate gas.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s:
Statement A : Natality refers to the birth of individuals in a population.
Statement B : Natality rate is expressed as the number of individuals produced per female per unit time.
o: Both statements A and B are true
Both statements A and B are false
Statement A is true, but statement B is false
Statement A is false, but statement B is true
questions.x: Natality is the production of new individuals by birth, and the key accepts natality rate expressed as offspring produced per female per unit time. Both statements are true.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: How does In-situ bioremediation differ from ex-situ bioremediation ?
o: It is more expensive and involves transport of contaminants
It treats contaminated material directly at the site
It uses chemicals instead of micro-organisms
questions.x: In-situ bioremediation treats the contamination where it lies, without digging it up. Ex-situ methods excavate or pump the material for treatment elsewhere.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: Population density is generally expressed as
o: The total number of individuals in a population
The number of individuals per unit area
The geographic distribution of the population
The number of individuals within a sample area
questions.x: Population density is the number of individuals per unit area (or volume) of habitat.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: Disease transmitting vector is not a Mosquito for which disease ?
questions.x: Leishmaniasis (kala-azar) is spread by sandflies. Chikungunya, dengue and malaria are mosquito-borne.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: What is a global issue associated with the trans-boundary movement of waste ?
o: Physical transfer of hazardous waste for reprocessing or storage
questions.x: The trans-boundary waste problem is the shipment of hazardous waste, often from rich to poor countries, for reprocessing or dumping. The Basel Convention regulates it.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: What can be considered a natural source of air pollution ?
questions.x: Forest fires, like volcanoes and dust storms, are natural sources of air pollution. The other options are human-made sources.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: Autonomous institute under the Department of Biotechnology (DBT)
o: Centre for Innovative and Applied Bioprocessing
Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology
questions.x: The Centre for Innovative and Applied Bioprocessing at Mohali is a DBT autonomous institute. CFTRI, CGCRI and CCMB are CSIR laboratories.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s:
Match List - I with List - II and choose the correct answer using the codes given below. (Common codes for English and Telugu Versions)
List - I (Emerging Technology) / List - II (Scientist)
a. Artificial Intelligence - I. Kevin Ashton
b. Open-AI - II. Sam Altman
c. Internet of Things (IoT) - III. Thomas P. Caudell
d. Augmented reality - IV. Alan Turing
questions.x: Alan Turing is linked with the foundations of AI, Sam Altman with OpenAI, Kevin Ashton coined 'Internet of Things', and Thomas Caudell coined 'augmented reality'.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: Radio Astronomy center is located in
questions.x: TIFR's Radio Astronomy Centre, with the Ooty Radio Telescope, is at Udhagamandalam (Ooty) in Tamil Nadu.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s:
Assertion (A) : DHRUVA is India's largest nuclear research reactor.
Reason (R) : Advanced Heavy Water Reactor envisages large scale utilization of plutonium bearing spent fuel.
o: (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.x: The 100 MW Dhruva at BARC is India's largest research reactor. The key treats (R) as incorrect, because the AHWR is designed mainly to use thorium (with plutonium/U-233 as driver fuel), not to make large-scale use of plutonium-bearing spent fuel.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s:
Assertion (A) : National Biofuel Coordination Committee needs to approve use of surplus food grains for production of ethanol for blending with petrol.
Reason (R) : Farmers are at risk of not getting appropriate price for their produce during the surplus production phase.
o: (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.x: The National Policy on Biofuels 2018 lets surplus food grains be used for ethanol only with NBCC approval, and it also notes that farmers risk low prices in surplus years. The key does not treat (R) as the reason for the approval requirement.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s:
Match List - I with List - II and choose the correct answer using the codes given below. (Common codes for English and Telugu Versions)
List - I (Solar Park) / List - II (Capacity in MW)
a. Hybrid Solar Wind Park Ramagiri - I. 1000
b. Ananthapuram-I Solar Park - II. 160
c. Kurnool Solar Park - III. 1500
d. Ananthapuram-II Solar Park - IV. 500
questions.x: APPSC's key pairs Ramagiri hybrid park with 160 MW, Ananthapuram-I with 1500 MW, Kurnool Ultra Mega Solar Park with 1000 MW and Ananthapuram-II with 500 MW.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: Project that is not associated with International Solar Alliance (ISA).
questions.x: PM-KUSUM is India's domestic scheme for solar pumps and farm solar plants. ISA initiatives include One Sun One World One Grid and the ISTAR-C training centres, and ISA capacity-building has used India's ITEC programme.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: State which is the largest producer of wind energy in India
questions.x: Gujarat has overtaken Tamil Nadu and now has the largest installed wind power capacity in India.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: Choose the correct statement.
o: Producers in an aquatic ecosystem are green plants
Archea are a type of producers who use energy from chemical compounds
Consumers are heterotrophs able to produce their food
The stability of ecosystem depends on consumers
questions.x: Chemosynthetic archaea, for example at deep-sea vents, are producers that use energy from inorganic chemical compounds. Aquatic producers are mainly phytoplankton rather than green plants, and consumers cannot make their own food.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s:
Match List - I with List - II and choose the correct answer using the codes given below. (Common codes for English and Telugu Versions)
List - I (Biotic factor) / List - II (Characteristic feature)
a. Humans - I. Recycling nutrients
b. Saprotrophs - II. Top order heterotrophs in food chain
c. Reptiles - III. Less urinating animal
d. Camel - IV. Stenothermal
questions.x: Humans are top-order heterotrophs, saprotrophs recycle nutrients, reptiles (cold-blooded) are treated as stenothermal, and camels conserve water by urinating very little.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: Forests that are located in mid latitude areas between tropics and polar region
questions.x: Temperate deciduous forests grow in the mid-latitudes between the tropical and polar zones, in regions with distinct seasons.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s:
Assertion (A) : Grazing food chain begins with dead leaves via herbivores to carnivores.
Reason (R) : In grazing food chain autotrophs capture energy and transfer to herbivores.
o: (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.x: The grazing food chain starts with living green plants (autotrophs) that pass energy to herbivores; chains starting from dead leaves are detritus food chains. So (A) is wrong and (R) is right.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: Biogeochemical cycle in which the main reservoir is not the soil
questions.x: APPSC's key marks the sulphur cycle, treating sediments and rocks rather than soil as its main store. The key is debatable, since the nitrogen cycle's main reservoir is clearly the atmosphere.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: CR in IUCN red list refers to
questions.x: In the IUCN Red List, CR means Critically Endangered, the highest risk category short of extinction in the wild (EW).
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: State that produces highest solid waste in India
questions.x: According to CPCB data, Maharashtra generates the most municipal solid waste of any State in India.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s:
Match the List - I with List - II and choose the correct answer using the codes given below. (Common codes for English and Telugu Versions)
List - I (Type of Solid Waste Management) / List - II (Function)
a. Incineration - I. Conversion of recyclable waste to carbon based fuels
b. Pyrolysis - II. Process of burning waste
c. Plasma gasification - III. Exposing waste to extremely high temperature
d. Composting - IV. Process of decaying organic waste biologically
questions.x: Incineration burns waste, pyrolysis converts waste into carbon-based fuels without oxygen, plasma gasification uses extremely high temperatures, and composting decays organic waste biologically.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: Which of these is not a biodegradable waste ?
questions.x: Tin is a metal that microorganisms cannot break down. Peels, fruit and wool are organic and biodegradable.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: Reason for the melting of Gangothri glaciers of Himalayas
questions.x: The retreat of Himalayan glaciers such as Gangotri is attributed mainly to global warming, that is, rising temperatures.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: Pollutant produced by vehicles that reduces the Oxygen carrying capacity of Blood
questions.x: Carbon monoxide binds to haemoglobin about 200 times more strongly than oxygen, forming carboxyhaemoglobin and cutting the blood's oxygen-carrying capacity.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s:
Assertion (A) : CFCs are greenhouse gases that contribute to climate change and increase UV radiation on earth.
Reason (R) : Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) are man made gases used in refrigerators, air conditioners and aerosol sprays.
o: (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.x: CFCs are potent greenhouse gases and also deplete ozone, letting more UV reach the earth. They are man-made refrigerants and propellants, but that use does not explain their climate effect.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s:
Match List - I with List - II and choose the correct answer using the codes given below. (Common codes for English and Telugu Versions)
List - I (Pollution) / List - II (Pollutant)
a. Marble Cancer - I. Methane
b. Biomagnification - II. Nickel
c. Green house effect - III. Sulphur dioxide and nitrogen dioxide
d. Lung cancer - IV. Chlorohydrocarbons
questions.x: Acid rain from SO2 and NO2 causes 'marble cancer', chlorinated hydrocarbons such as DDT biomagnify, methane is a greenhouse gas, and nickel compounds are linked to lung cancer.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: Choose the incorrect statement.
o: CO2 is continuously being released because of human activities
Deforestation is decreasing the amount of CO2
Oil spillage causes oxygen depletion and distress to aquatic animals
Burning of plastic reduces the germination of seeds in crop fields
questions.x: Deforestation increases atmospheric CO2, because fewer trees absorb it and cleared biomass releases it.
questions.subject: Science & Technology

questions.s: Anganwadi worker is a functionary of which scheme ?
questions.x: Anganwadi workers run Anganwadi centres under the Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) scheme, started in 1975.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
